correctness.rationale: The normalized identity starting block gives mean Ritz node mu. The Hermite interpolant is the tangent 2/mu-x/mu^2. The exact two-level identity A=(a+b)I-ab A^(-1) reduces the residual matrix to alpha A^(-1)+beta I, and constant sign-vector norm gives the centered samplewise estimator identity. Scalar differentiation, factorization and a multiplicity extremum establish all strict and equality boundaries. An exact-rational standalone checker enumerates 8184 sign vectors over 84 parameterized matrix configurations; the analytic proof handles all n and s.

originality.rationale: The examined 2026 global-Lanczos paper proves a general correction representation and a general Rademacher variance identity, but does not give the special two-point minimal-polynomial scalar reduction, exact multiplicity-dependent risk phase, first amplification dimension seven, or the all-probe exact cancellation contrast. Those specific phase boundaries do not follow from the cited results merely as a substitution of displayed constants; their derivation requires the two-eigenvalue algebra and a sharp optimization over positive contrast and multiplicities. Related deflation and randomized Krylov estimators do not give an identical estimator or a theorem implying these boundaries. Searches found no matching result; historical priority remains subject to external verification.
residual_risks: Generic earlier control-variate and interpolation literature could have independently derived the same two-point algebra; searches do not prove historical uniqueness.
One related diagonal-interpolation paper was available for scope comparison at abstract level rather than a complete method inspection.
The result is for a narrow one-node, two-level, exact-inverse Rademacher setting; no broader performance claim is made.

value.rationale: The new global Lanczos source motivates stochastic correction as a variance reduction. The exact n=7 onset of variance regression, optimal contrast and 625/576 witness, arbitrary-dimension worst-case factor, and opposite zero-variance contrast, together with Frobenius-norm improvement in the variance-inflation example, give a concrete algorithm-selection boundary for a natural two-spectrum matrix class. This is structurally different from generic unbiasedness or an unmotivated special matrix computation, and makes no runtime or broad-spectrum extrapolation.
